summary: Batch retry coordination causing duplicate external webhook posts when orchestration truncates batch idempotency token
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook deliveries from their orchestration service when using batched function calls across Python and Go SDK clients. The orchestrator generates a per-batch idempotency token which is attached as an HTTP header. An edge proxy in the customer's network truncates headers longer than ~128 bytes. When retries occur (exponential backoff with jitter), the orchestrator resends the batched request but with a truncated idempotency header in some retry paths, which the webhook router treats as a different token and re-executes downstream jobs.

Impact:
- Duplicated webhook deliveries to 3rd-party endpoints, causing duplicate side-effects (duplicate invoices, duplicate task creation).
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity; visible in production traffic.
- Billing and downstream partner complaints reported.

Environment:
- prod us-east (dedicated cluster)
- SDKs: python 1.9.4 (multiprocess worker pool), go 0.8.2 (orchestration worker)
- Edge proxy: customer-managed HAProxy layer truncating headers at ~128 bytes

Observed frequency:
- Occurs under moderate retry rates and when batch idempotency token length >120 bytes. Approximately 1 in 200 retried batches result in duplication in customer logs.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should preserve idempotency semantics: identical logical batch should not cause duplicate downstream executions even when header transport is lossy.

Actual behavior:
- Partial header truncation causes token normalization mismatch between initial request and retry; webhook router treats them as distinct tokens and replays downstream tool invocations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Orchestrator constructs a batched function call payload for N=10 user tasks and computes a per-batch idempotency nonce (UUID + HMAC + metadata).
2) Attaches the nonce in X-Redwood-Idempotency header (base64-encoded, typically ~140 bytes).
3) Sends batch via Python SDK client behind customer edge proxy to Redwood API. Initial request succeeds or times out.
4) Orchestrator triggers retry on exponential backoff; some retries are routed through a different HAProxy instance with stricter header length limits, which truncates the header to ~96 bytes.
5) Redwood webhook router receives the retried request with truncated header and does not match the original idempotency record, so it re-executes downstream webhooks.
logs: 2026-03-09T18:22:14Z [redwood-webhook-router] received X-Redwood-Idempotency=base64_truncated -- no match found -- executing webhooks
2026-03-09T18:22:14Z [redwood-serving-runtime] function_call id=fc-9933 delivered to customer endpoint https://hooks.partner.example.com/create-task response=200
customer_report: Customer provided example trace and downstream duplicate webhook bodies. They are willing to test with a shorter idempotency token or switch to body-based idempotency but require vendor guidance and a recommended mitigation path.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Lena Ortiz (reporter): Added cluster traces and sample headers. Noticed Python multiprocess client sometimes sends retries that look different from the Go worker retries.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Samir Patel (assignee): Acknowledged ticket, asked for full raw request/response headers and whether customer can reproduce with a synthetic load. Assigned to eng-sdks to validate header canonicalization.

2026-03-11 15:20 - Eng-SDKs (Emma Zhou): Reproduced locally with a header length cutoff at 100 bytes. Observed our idempotency lookup keyed solely on raw header value; truncation leads to mismatches. Opened PR to canonicalize idempotency token source (pulling from body when header absent/too-short).

2026-03-12 10:30 - Customer (Acme AI - infra): Confirmed they can temporarily increase HAProxy header buffer to stop truncation but prefer longer-term SDK/platform fix because they cannot guarantee uniform proxies across regions.

2026-03-13 09:05 - Samir Patel: Proposed mitigation and put together rollout plan for a backward-compatible change to idempotency matching: prefer full header but fallback to canonical body-derived token when header shorter than expected. Tagged related PR for canary rollout in us-east-1.
2026-03-14 08:55 - Eng-Oncall (Miguel Torres): Canary deployment scheduled for 2026-03-15 into a small subset of requests; monitoring dashboard and trace sampling added.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: header truncation at edge -> mismatch in idempotency key -> duplicate execution.
Verified: local ha-proxy simulation truncates header, Redwood lookup fails because we use header-as-is to index idempotency store (Redis).

Confirmed cross-SDK behavior: Python multiprocess clients and Go worker retries are both susceptible because token is generated by orchestrator and transported via header. Not an SDK bug per-se, but SDKs can help by offering body-based fallback token generation and clearer guidance.
Risk: Changing idempotency matching risks false dedupe if bodies evolve between retries; must ensure canonicalization uses stable fields (batch id + digest) and include a TTL/namespace.
action_items: 1) Short-term customer mitigation: increase HAProxy header buffer and/or move idempotency token into request body (POST field) instead of header.
2) Medium-term platform fix: implement fallback idempotency matching (canonical body digest) with feature flag and canary rollout.
3) SDK guidance: publish best-practices note for orchestrators to keep canonical idempotency tokens <= 100 bytes or use body-based tokens. Add examples in Python/Go SDK docs.
4) Create follow-up internal ticket to add explicit telemetry when header length != expected length so we can detect edge truncation without full customer trace.
resolution: Workaround provided: customer increased HAProxy header limits and temporarily moved idempotency token to a JSON body field. Engineering implemented a canary-ready change to accept a canonical body-derived idempotency token when the header is missing or shorter than expected. Canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 in us-east, monitoring in place. Post-canary, we'll roll out globally and publish SDK/docs guidance. Customer is satisfied with the mitigation path pending canary results.
follow_up: Post-canary: publish a short KB article with recommended token formats and SDK snippets for Python/Go/TS. Add a detection metric for truncated idempotency headers and surface as alert to support.
workaround_steps: A) Increase header buffer on HAProxy: set 'tune.bufsize' to 16384 and 'tune.maxrewrite' to 1024
B) If changing proxy not possible, include 'idempotency_token' in POST JSON body and add 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Fallback: body' header so platform knows to derive key from body digest.
C) For Python multi-process clients, ensure consistent generation of nonce in parent process and pass via IPC to workers to avoid per-process variation.
